# `plot2`

**[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) + `ggplot2` =
[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)**

`ggplot2` composes any plot from layers, aesthetics, scales, coordinates
and themes. This grammar makes it flexible and precise, but it also
means that a plot often requires many functions and arguments: a plot of
“counts per department, coloured by year” requires knowledge of
[`geom_col()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_bar.html),
`aes(fill = )`,
[`position_dodge()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/position_dodge.html),
`scale_fill_*()` and
[`theme()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html), and of
the data steps that come before them.

`plot2` takes the opposite approach. Like base R’s
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html), one call gives
a complete plot, even when the type of plot is not given. You describe
what you want to see, and
[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)
summarises, sorts and labels the data, and chooses the plot type,
colours, axes and theme:

``` r

iris |> plot2(x = Species, y = mean(Sepal.Length))
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-2-1.png)

The result is a standard `ggplot` object, so every `ggplot2` function
and extension still works on it.

## Installation

`plot2` is not on CRAN yet. Install it from r-universe:

``` r

install.packages("plot2", repos = c("https://msberends.r-universe.dev",
                                    "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

## The same plot, two ways

A sorted column plot of the number of cars per class, with data labels.
The data set `mpg` comes with `ggplot2`.

``` r

# ggplot2, dplyr and forcats
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)

mpg |>
  count(class) |>
  mutate(class = fct_reorder(class, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = class, y = n)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Vehicle class", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

``` r

# plot2
library(plot2)

mpg |> plot2(x = class, y = n(), x.sort = "freq-asc")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-5-1.png)

Both give a sorted column plot with data labels.
[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md) sets
the axis titles, the theme and the axis expansion by itself.

## What plot2 replaces

| Task | ggplot2 | plot2 |
|----|----|----|
| Summarise, then plot | [`group_by()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/group_by.html) + [`summarise()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/summarise.html) + [`ggplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html) + [`geom_col()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_bar.html) | `plot2(x = a, y = mean(b))` |
| Sort bars | `mutate(fct_reorder(...))` | `x.sort = "freq-desc"` |
| Group by colour | `aes(fill = var)` for bars, `aes(colour = var)` for points, each with its own `scale_*()` | `category = var` |
| Set colours | `scale_fill_manual(values = ...)` or `scale_colour_manual(values = ...)`, depending on the geom | `colour = c(...)` |
| Facet | `+ facet_wrap(~var)` | `facet = var` |
| Data labels | `+ geom_text(aes(label = ...), vjust = ...)` | automatic for columns |
| Stacked bars | `geom_col(position = "stack")` or `position = "fill"` | `stacked = TRUE` or `stacked_fill = TRUE` |

## Plot types

[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)
supports all `ggplot2` geoms, and adds plot types such as dumbbell,
back-to-back, Sankey, spider and UpSet plots. Each plot below is made
with a single line of code:

![Plot types of plot2()](reference/figures/plot_types.png)

Plot types of plot2()

## Examples

The four plotting directions `x`, `y`, `category` and `facet` describe
most plots. They accept columns and calculations:

``` r

admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = age_group, y = n(), category = gender, facet = ward)
#> Using free y scales per facet since the two y scales differ by 25% or more (use facet.fixed_y = TRUE for the same scale in all facets)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-6-1.png)

Titles can be calculated from the data as well:

``` r

mtcars |>
  plot2(x = mpg,
        y = hp,
        category = factor(cyl),
        category.title = "Cylinders",
        title = paste("Horsepower of", n(), "cars"))
#> Using type = "point" since both axes are numeric
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-7-1.png)

A correlation matrix becomes a heatmap:

``` r

mtcars |>
  cor() |>
  plot2(datalabels = TRUE,
        colour = c("steelblue", "white", "firebrick"),
        category.title = "Correlation")
#> Assuming type = "tile" since the matrix contains identical row and column names
#> Using category.midpoint = 0 (the current category scale centre)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-8-1.png)

## Learning more

- [Introduction to
  plot2](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/articles/plot2.html)
  ([`vignette("plot2", package = "plot2")`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/articles/plot2.md))
  describes the main ideas.
- [Plot
  types](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/articles/supported_types.html)
  ([`vignette("supported_types", package = "plot2")`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/articles/supported_types.md))
  shows every plot type.
- The [package website](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/) has articles
  on colours and themes, maps, fonts, and
  [`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md) for
  `ggplot2` users.

[`create_interactively()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/create_interactively.md)
opens a Shiny app that builds a plot from a point-and-click interface
and shows the code:

``` r

iris |> create_interactively()
```

![The Shiny app of
create_interactively()](reference/figures/create_interactively.jpg)

The Shiny app of create_interactively()

# Package index

## Creating plots

[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)
creates a complete plot from data in one call. Its methods accept data
frames, vectors, tables, formulas, matrices, models and geographic data.
[`add_type()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
and its shortcuts add layers to a plot.

- [`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md) :

  Conveniently Create a New `ggplot`

- [`plot2(`*`<default>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  [`plot2(`*`<formula>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  [`plot2(`*`<freq>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  [`plot2(`*`<sf>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  [`plot2(`*`<data.frame>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  [`plot2(`*`<matrix>`*`)`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-methods.md)
  :

  Methods for
  [`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)

- [`add_type()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_line()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_point()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_col()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_errorbar()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_smooth()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  [`add_sf()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_type.md)
  : Add Plot Element

## Changing plots

Change the mapping or the order of the layers of an existing plot, or
use the coordinate system of spider plots.

- [`add_mapping()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/add_mapping.md)
  : Add Additional Mapping

- [`move_layer()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/move_layer.md)
  :

  Move a `ggplot` Layer

- [`coord_spider()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/coord_spider.md)
  [`CoordSpider`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/coord_spider.md)
  : Spider (Radar) Coordinate System for ggplot2

## Colours

Get colours from names and palettes, and register the colours of an
organisation for use in all plots.

- [`get_colour()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/colour.md)
  [`register_colour()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/colour.md)
  [`unregister_colour()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/colour.md)
  [`add_white()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/colour.md)
  :

  Get (and Register) Colours from R, Viridis and More

## Themes, titles and labels

The default theme of
[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md),
markdown in titles, and labelling functions for axes and data labels.

- [`theme_minimal2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/theme_minimal2.md)
  : An Even More Minimal Theme
- [`md_to_expression()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/md_to_expression.md)
  : Convert Markdown to Plotmath Expression
- [`get_plot_title()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/get_plot_title.md)
  : Get Plot Title
- [`euros()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/labellers.md)
  [`dollars()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/labellers.md)
  : Label Currencies
- [`label_taxonomy()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/label_taxonomy.md)
  : Label Taxonomic Names in Italics

## Number formatting

The decimal mark and thousands separator, determined from the session or
set with options.

- [`dec_mark()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/dec_mark.md)
  [`big_mark()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/dec_mark.md)
  : Use Decimal Comma?

## Interactive use

Convert a plot to an interactive `plotly` widget, or build a plot in a
Shiny app.

- [`as_plotly()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plotly.md)
  [`plotly_style()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plotly.md)
  : Create Interactive Plotly

- [`create_interactively()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/create_interactively.md)
  :

  Interactively Create a `plot2`

## Options

Package options that set defaults for all plots in a session.

- [`plot2-options`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2-options.md)
  :

  [`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md)
  Options

## Data sets

Example data sets used in the documentation.

- [`admitted_patients`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/admitted_patients.md)
  : Example Data Set with Admitted Patients
- [`netherlands`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/netherlands.md)
  : Example Geography Data Set: the Netherlands

## Re-exported functions

Functions from `dplyr` and `tidyselect` that are often used in the
arguments of
[`plot2()`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/plot2.md).

- [`reexports`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`%>%`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`n`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`n_distinct`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`everything`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`starts_with`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`ends_with`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`matches`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`where`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`first`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`last`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`all_of`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md)
  [`any_of`](https://msberends.github.io/plot2/reference/reexports.md) :
  Objects exported from other packages
